title: A $750K Horror Film Just Beat The Mummy in India. Obsession Is the Sleeper Nobody Saw Coming — and It Won't Stop Winning.
excerpt: Made for the price of a single Bollywood item number, Curry Barker's supernatural thriller has crossed $260 million worldwide and become the third highest-grossing Hollywood release of 2026 in India. The diaspora can't look away.
body:
It started as the kind of film studios bury on a quiet weekend. No stars you'd recognise. A first-time-ish director. A budget — $750,000 — that wouldn't cover the catering on a Yash Raj set. And then **Obsession** did the thing nobody scripts: it refused to die.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=gMC8kkwbIQQ</youtube>

A month into its run, Curry Barker's supernatural horror thriller has grossed more than $260 million worldwide, shattering a record *The Blair Witch Project* held for twenty-six years as the highest-grossing film ever made for under a million dollars. But the number that should make Mumbai sit up is the Indian one. **Obsession** has now amassed ₹59 crore at the India net box office, vaulting past Hollywood heavyweights *The Mummy* and *The Devil Wears Prada 2* to become the **third highest-grossing Hollywood release of 2026 in India**. Only *Project Hail Mary* and *Michael* sit ahead of it — both films with stars, marketing budgets, and the kind of pedigree this one simply doesn't have.

So what is everyone watching? The premise is pure, queasy fairy tale. **Michael Johnston** plays Bear, a lonely music-store clerk nursing a hopeless flame for his childhood crush Nikki, played by **Inde Navarrette**. He gets his hands on a supernatural trinket — a "One Wish Willow" he'd meant as a gift — and makes the wish every romantic comedy is secretly built on: that she'll love him more than anyone in the world. She does. That's the horror. Her affection curdles into a devouring fixation, her memories warp, and Bear spends the rest of the film trying to claw back a wish he should never have made.

> "A simple wish becomes a scary nightmare."

It's a 100-minute slow-tightening of the screws, and critics have been disarmed by it — a 94% on Rotten Tomatoes for a film that cost less than a Bandra two-bedroom. What's eerie about its box office isn't just the size, it's the shape. Horror films are supposed to front-load and collapse. **Obsession** did the opposite, jumping more than 30% in its second weekend and holding through weekdays on the strength of repeat viewings and the most valuable currency in cinema: people telling their friends they have to see it.

For the Indian diaspora, the appeal lands on two levels. There's the universal one — young audiences worldwide have made this a word-of-mouth ritual, the film you drag a group chat to. And there's the quietly desi one: a story about obsessive love that turns monstrous is not exactly foreign territory for an audience raised on *Darr*, *Anjaam*, and a hundred songs where devotion and danger share a verse. Bollywood has been mining the line between romance and obsession for decades. Hollywood just did it for the price of a wedding.

The success has, predictably, set off the sequel machine. Director **Curry Barker** — who wrote, directed, and edited the thing himself — is already being asked whether *Obsession 2* is coming, and the genre's gatekeepers are scrambling to find "the next Obsession," with an Australian supernatural chiller called *Leviticus* (a hair ahead at 96% on Rotten Tomatoes) being floated as the heir apparent. Blumhouse-adjacent producers know exactly what they have: proof, again, that audiences are starved for an original idea executed with conviction, and that they'll pay multiplex prices for it.

That last point should travel all the way to Film City. In a 2026 already defined in India by ₹3,000 IMAX tickets for Nolan's *The Odyssey* and an ageing roster of male superstars, **Obsession** is the inconvenient counter-argument — that spectacle and star power aren't the only routes to a packed hall. Sometimes a good, mean little story, told straight, does the work that ₹250 crore can't.

**Where to watch:** **Obsession** is still playing in theatres across the US, UK, and Canada, and remains in select Indian multiplexes after its May 29 India release. A streaming home hasn't been formally locked, but given its theatrical legs, expect a premium-VOD and digital window to follow once the box office finally cools — if it ever does. For now, the smart move is the one millions have already made: see it in the dark, with strangers, the way it was meant to curdle.
